SkyBridge Multi-Adviser Hedge Fund Portfolios, LLC (CIK 0001181848) is a real, SEC-registered fund-of-hedge-funds vehicle managed by SkyBridge Capital (Anthony Scaramucci's firm), publicly known for its exposure to FTX prior to FTX's November 2022 collapse. The FY2023 N-CSR (period ended 2023-03-31) discloses this directly and completely: FTX Trading Ltd. common and three preferred share classes, aggregate real cost $37,206,327, marked to real fair value $0 as of 2023-03-31 -- a genuine, disclosed total write-off, not a synthetic stress scenario. The fund's own disclosed one-year total return, -30.29% vs. its benchmark's -1.93%, is a real, severe, disclosed underperformance driven by this and other crypto-strategy positions (Brevan Howard, NYDIG, Multicoin, Polychain, Galaxy -- all real names in the same schedule, not selected here since they fall outside the top-8-by-cost cutoff). Top 8 positions were selected by ORIGINAL COST rather than current fair value (the convention used for fof-public-hlpaf-2026) specifically because sorting a stress case by post-loss fair value would silently exclude the FTX position (now $0) from the 'top' cut -- cost-based selection is the only ordering that surfaces both the fund's largest surviving winners (Point72, Axonic, Millennium, all real gains) and its largest real total loss (FTX) side by side, which is the entire point of an adversarial case. Position-level Commitment/Called/Distributed history is not disclosed (same real gap as fof-public-hlpaf-2026): Cost substitutes for Commitment/Called, Distributed stays 0. Strategy classification (Cryptocurrency and Digital Assets / Relative Value / Event Driven / Private Equity) IS disclosed per position in this filing, unlike HLPAF's schedule -- a real improvement over the prior case's 'n/a' gap. First Acquisition Date is disclosed per position (not a proxy). FoF-level NAV roll-forward figures (beginning/ending Shareholders' Capital, realized/unrealized loss, distributions, capital contributions) are all real, from the Consolidated Statements of Changes in Shareholders' Capital -- but this fund uses open-end/interval subscription-redemption mechanics (contributions + reinvested distributions + REDEMPTIONS), not the private-equity-style capital-call mechanics this domain's template models (calls + distributions only, no redemptions line) -- a real, structural mechanics mismatch, honestly disclosed as a limitation, expected to produce a materially larger NAV-roll-forward reconciliation residual than fof-public-hlpaf-2026's fee-model mismatch alone.
